topic:
Sharp optimal-personalized-treatment-value estimation with jointly growing treatment menus and sparse categorical patient groups. For every n>=1,d>=1,K>=2, observe n iid (X,A,Y), X in [d], A in [K], Y binary, under consistency and conditional exchangeability. Allow arbitrary unknown masses p_x, unrestricted conditional outcome means mu_ax in [0,1], and unknown propensities with sum_a e_ax=1 and 1/(2K)<=e_ax<=2/K on positive-mass cells; null cells, exact ties and boundary means are legal. Target Vstar=sum_x p_x max_a mu_ax and R(n,d,K)=inf over all estimators sup over this law class of mean squared error. Derive an explicit all-regime rate, including every logarithm, transition and saturation branch, bounded above and below by R with absolute constants independent of n,d,K. Construct a total computable attaining estimator and matching same-class all-estimator converse. Determine necessary and sufficient consistency and parametric-MSE conditions for arbitrary dimension sequences. The exact rate and estimator mechanics are outputs; an unevaluated optimization or fixed-K constants do not solve the kernel. Preserve unknown masses and logging in the upper bound; known-uniform lower subexperiments are legal. Recover d=1 and K=2 benchmarks independently, without replacing the full joint theorem by those slices or the presolved K>=d^2 region. Consumer: the unrestricted attainable-value benchmark for maq/grf multi-arm treatment targeting as intervention menus expand; this does not replace learned-policy inference or claim a full budget-curve result. The legal d=2,K=3 unequal-propensity witness has Vstar=43/50 with switching maximizing arms. Put the dimension-uniform approximation/variance and matching mixture geometry in the headline; do not silently narrow or downgrade if it fails.

PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A centered random winner in every patient group yields an exact fixed-sample likelihood-mixture identity with a binomial count of coinciding winners. Its derived lower risk is c min{1,dK log(1+sqrt(K/d))/n}; a total empirical cell-weighted maximum has upper risk C min{1,dK log(eK)/n} on the full unknown-mass and unknown-propensity class. These match for K>=d^2. The one-group passive benchmark and a grouped-arm reduction to the binary parent also yield the bounded-d-and-K parametric criterion. Small exact likelihood calculations passed; null cells, ties, boundary means, unequal logging, saturation, adaptive best-mean prior art, and the known-logging Bayes-accuracy reduction were checked. These are unverified derivations, not a solved full frontier.
UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Open Lemma J must jointly control approximation bias, factorial covariance, and normalized moment-prior separation with absolute constants, closing 2<K<d^2 and the full consistency boundary for arbitrary masses and propensities.
EARLY KILL TEST: Test the first certificate on the K=64 Boolean slice at degrees 4,7,8 and compute its exact lifted variance. A verified dual bound or rigorous OR obstruction must support any refutation; floating-point LP output alone cannot. Stop a route that hides K in its constants.
STRONGEST-FORM DRAFT (unverified, gaps listed inside): <repo-root>/internal/presolve_drafts/stat_manyarm_optimal_value_joint_frontier.md.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine the sharp all-regime minimax MSE for unrestricted optimal-treatment value when both the number of categorical patient groups d and treatment count K grow, including sparse cells, unknown propensities of order 1/K, arbitrary masses, and multiway ties.

source_refs.excerpt: Vanishing overlap, growing treatment count, and sharp leading constants remain outside the theorem.
both the vertex-adaptive approximation inequality and the centered coefficient envelope

source_refs.claim: The optimal-treatment value is nonregular at laws with nonunique optimal treatments; the paper gives asymptotic online one-step inference, not a growing-d,K finite-sample minimax frontier.
source_refs.author: Alexander R. Luedtke and Mark J. van der Laan

source_refs.claim: HAVER gives instance-dependent MSE upper bounds for the passive one-group maximum-mean problem, rather than the grouped causal all-estimator minimax frontier.
source_refs.author: Tuan Nguyen, Jay Barrett, and Kwang-Sung Jun

source_refs.claim: Multi-action observational policy learning obtains minimax policy-regret results for restricted policy classes, a different object from MSE estimation of unrestricted optimal value.
source_refs.author: Zhengyuan Zhou, Susan Athey, and Stefan Wager

open_problems.why_unsolved: The closest banked theorem treats binary treatment, where the nonsmooth component reduces to one absolute-value tie diagonal. The literature otherwise separates fixed-dimensional nonregular inference, restricted-class policy regret, fixed-policy evaluation, and one-group maximum-mean upper bounds. With K treatments, intersections of many tie faces replace the binary diagonal, while arbitrary p_x and unknown e_ax create random sparse denominators. A resolution must make the approximation bias, centered-factorial covariance, and lower-mixture geometry dimension-uniform and mutually matching; fixed-K constants and separate one-group or binary slices cannot establish the joint frontier.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: An explicit piecewise rate r(n,d,K), including every logarithmic, transition, and saturation branch, with a total estimator satisfying worst-case MSE at most C r and an all-estimator lower bound at least c r for absolute c,C, plus necessary-and-sufficient consistency and O(1/n)-MSE conditions for arbitrary dimension sequences.

writing_exemplar.why: Its motivation moves directly from optimal personalized-treatment value to the maximum functional's nondifferentiability and a concrete statistical response.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Personalized treatment requires knowing attainable optimal value -> maximizing over actions creates a nondifferentiable functional -> expanding menus and sparse patient groups require an exact dimension-uniform minimax benchmark.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt HAVER's lower-confidence pivot, data-dependent head set, weighted averaging, and tail-integral MSE proof.
method_exemplars.why_closest: At d=1 the target is exactly passive maximum-mean estimation; the full theorem must add random causal cell counts and aggregation over groups.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer the nonsmooth/smooth split, factorial-moment estimation of polynomial approximants, clipping, and fuzzy-hypothesis lower bounds.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both problems estimate a high-dimensional nonsmooth functional from sparse multinomial observations, but the summand here is a K-variate maximum with random normalization.

method_exemplars.technique: Use approximation–moment duality so the estimator bias and least-favorable-mixture separation depend on the same extremal quantity.
method_exemplars.why_closest: A matched joint d,K frontier requires the upper approximation and lower mixture geometry to retain identical dimension dependence.

open_problems.open_problem: Establish a dimension-uniform approximation-versus-variance and dual-mixture certificate for the K-ary maximum after factorial-moment lifting under multinomial treatment logging, especially for 2<K<d^2.

source_refs.claim: Near-best polynomial approximation and factorial moments solve additive nonsmooth discrete-functional problems, but do not supply a K-variate maximum certificate with multinomial covariance control.
source_refs.author: Jiantao Jiao, Kartik Venkat, Yanjun Han, and Tsachy Weissman

source_refs.claim: Best polynomial approximation drives both the estimator and a dual moment-matching lower bound for large-alphabet entropy, yielding matched all-regime rates and a consistency threshold.
source_refs.author: Yihong Wu and Pengkun Yang

source_refs.claim: Moment-matched priors and chi-square control yield sharp lower bounds for a nonsmooth functional and are paired with an approximation-theoretic estimator.
source_refs.author: T. Tony Cai and Mark G. Low

source_refs.claim: Approximate degree is characterized for symmetric Boolean functions; the OR slice imposes a square-root-dimension obstruction relevant to Boolean restrictions of the maximum.
source_refs.author: Ramamohan Paturi

open_problems.why_unsolved: Available statistical approximation machinery is primarily univariate and additive, while Boolean approximate-degree results control uniform error without controlling the variance of an unbiased factorial lift. The first proof step that changes is replacing a scalar approximant by a permutation-symmetric multivariate approximant to max(z_1,...,z_K), then bounding every covariance term induced by shared multinomial totals and normalization. The dual object must also become valid probability priors with matched mixed moments and absolute-constant mixture-distance control. The supplied Lemma J claim is unverified; a resolution must independently prove the certificate or provide a rigorous OR-slice obstruction rather than relying on floating-point optimization.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A proved primal-dual theorem giving an explicit degree-L K-variate maximum approximant with uniform error and an absolute-constant variance bound for its factorial-moment lift, together with normalized moment-matched priors whose target separation and likelihood-mixture distance yield the same intermediate-regime rate.

writing_exemplar.why: It connects sparse high-dimensional sampling, plug-in failure, and approximation theory as the common mechanism behind construction and converse.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Sparse sampling makes plug-in bias dominant -> nonsmooth regions require estimable polynomial surrogates -> the K-ary causal maximum requires a dimension-uniform approximation and lifted-variance certificate.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer the duality between best uniform approximation and moment-matched fuzzy hypotheses, including control of the resulting mixture experiment.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The desired result likewise needs one approximation object to certify both the attainable estimator and the matching converse.

method_exemplars.technique: Transfer low-moment prior matching, chi-square control of induced mixtures, and unbiased polynomial estimation of a kinked functional.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It is the closest sharp template for turning a polynomial-approximation modulus into both sides of a nonsmooth minimax theorem.

method_exemplars.technique: Use symmetrization and the approximate-degree lower bound for OR as a rigorous obstruction test for proposed low-degree maximum approximants.
method_exemplars.why_closest: On Boolean mean configurations the K-ary maximum becomes OR, so any statistical certificate must respect this approximation-theoretic barrier.

open_problems.open_problem: For K bounded Bernoulli arms observed passively with balanced or overlap-comparable sample counts, characterize the exact all-K minimax MSE, including saturation, for estimating max_a mu_a rather than identifying the best arm.

source_refs.claim: HAVER gives precise instance-dependent MSE upper bounds for maximum-mean estimation but does not claim a matching global minimax lower bound over bounded Bernoulli means.
source_refs.author: Tuan Nguyen, Jay Barrett, and Kwang-Sung Jun

source_refs.claim: Maximum sample averages are positively biased, cross-validation is negatively biased, and no unbiased maximum-value estimator exists in general.
source_refs.author: Hado van Hasselt

source_refs.claim: Gaussian-weighted maximum-value estimation is analyzed via separate bias and variance bounds rather than a matched minimax MSE theorem.
source_refs.author: Carlo D'Eramo, Marcello Restelli, and Alessandro Nuara

open_problems.why_unsolved: HAVER supplies strong worst-case and gap-dependent upper guarantees, whereas older maximum-value methods mostly bound bias and variance separately. The scan located no converse matching the best passive estimator uniformly over K, sample size, ties, boundary Bernoulli means, and saturation. Gaussian selected-mean theory does not automatically cover the bounded parameter boundary, while best-arm-identification lower bounds concern the maximizer's identity rather than its value. This benchmark must be solved independently before it can serve as a valid d=1 reduction of the joint causal theorem.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A closed-form rate r_1(N,K), a total Bernoulli maximum-mean estimator with worst-case MSE at most C r_1, and a bounded-parameter mixture or constrained-risk lower bound at least c r_1 for every N and K.

writing_exemplar.why: It cleanly distinguishes estimation of the largest mean value from best-arm identification and formulates explicit MSE objectives.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Many-action decisions require the value of the best arm -> the empirical maximum suffers optimizer's-curse bias -> a matched minimax theorem is needed to determine the passive benchmark.

method_exemplars.technique: Use its lower-confidence pivot and head-averaging construction, together with exact tail integration, as the upper-bound mechanism.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It estimates precisely max_a mu_a under passive samples and is the nearest MSE-controlled construction.

method_exemplars.technique: Construct moment-matched priors, control chi-square distance between observation mixtures, and relate functional separation to best polynomial approximation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The maximum is a nonsmooth symmetric functional, so a sharp converse must conceal mean configurations while separating their maximum values.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether a cell-weighted HAVER-style head-averaging estimator attains the grouped causal optimal-value minimax rate under unknown overlap-bounded logging and multinomial patient-group counts, including unobserved groups and arms.

source_refs.claim: HAVER handles passive, externally supplied and possibly unequal arm sample sizes, but has no random-context masses or causal logging layer.
source_refs.author: Tuan Nguyen, Jay Barrett, and Kwang-Sung Jun

source_refs.claim: For fixed-policy contextual-bandit evaluation, minimax MSE bounds are matched up to constants by logging-aware estimators, avoiding the data-dependent maximizing action.
source_refs.author: Yu-Xiang Wang, Alekh Agarwal, and Miroslav Dudik

source_refs.claim: Finite-time minimax risk is characterized for fixed-policy off-policy evaluation in bandits, with regression estimation near-minimax up to an action-dependent constant.
source_refs.author: Lihong Li, Remi Munos, and Csaba Szepesvari

source_refs.claim: Efficiency bounds and attaining estimators for multiple logging policies show that logging structure changes optimal weighting, but the target policy is fixed.
source_refs.author: Nathan Kallus, Yuta Saito, and Masatoshi Uehara

open_problems.why_unsolved: HAVER conditions on externally supplied arm totals, so its first proof step must change to a joint event decomposition over random N_x and N_xa, estimated group masses, and logging probabilities. Fixed-policy off-policy evaluation controls inverse-propensity variance but avoids the data-dependent maximizing action. Applying an arm estimator independently inside every group fails on null cells and may lose dimension factors when the estimates are aggregated. Searches combining head averaging, multinomial cell occupancy, and causal optimal value did not surface an occupied result.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A fully specified cell-weighted head-averaging or hybrid estimator, defined for every count array including N_x=0 and N_xa=0, with a uniform nonasymptotic MSE theorem and a matching lower bound identifying precisely when random occupancy changes the one-group rate.

writing_exemplar.why: It makes multi-action observational assignment, overlap, and computational feasibility central to the problem formulation.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Observed patient data contain many possible actions -> logging controls which action outcomes appear in each context -> sharp attainable-value estimation must survive random sparse cell counts.

method_exemplars.technique: Lift its lower-confidence pivot, comparable-width candidate set, count-weighted head average, and tail-event MSE calculation to each patient group.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Conditional on one populated group, the causal subproblem is HAVER's passive maximum-mean problem.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt its logging-aware MSE decomposition and SWITCH thresholding to select between direct cell regression and inverse-propensity correction.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It provides a nearby finite-sample treatment of logged action availability, although only for fixed policies.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt variance-minimizing weighting across logging strata and the accompanying efficiency calculation.
method_exemplars.why_closest: Both settings aggregate strata with heterogeneous effective propensities, but the destination additionally maximizes within each stratum.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct a polynomial-time, numerically stable estimator attaining the many-arm categorical optimal-value minimax rate without enumerating auxiliary markings or exponentially many tensor coefficients.

source_refs.excerpt: no polynomial-time or numerically stable implementation guarantee
State a computational representation or complexity bound for evaluating the conditional Rao–Blackwellization
Add a computational corollary with a finite certified approximation routine and explicit complexity

open_problems.why_unsolved: Even for K=2, the accepted estimator is explicit only as a measurable Rao–Blackwellized rule; its conditional averaging and tensor-polynomial coefficient calculation have no practical complexity or stability guarantee. Growing K makes direct tensor expansion exponential and can hide menu size in arithmetic constants. The first proof step that changes is the representation of the local polynomial lift: it must permit evaluation and variance accounting through a compressed basis, recurrence, unbiased sketch, or certified sparse expansion while preserving the coefficient envelope used in the risk proof.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A total algorithm with runtime and bit complexity polynomial in n,d,K and the requested numerical precision, accompanied by a finite-sample MSE bound matching the statistical minimax rate up to absolute constants.

writing_exemplar.why: It presents a nonsmooth large-alphabet estimator as an implementable construction tied directly to its minimax guarantee.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Plug-in maxima are biased in sparse cells -> polynomial estimators can recover information-theoretic gains -> many-arm tensor growth threatens computability -> compress the construction without losing its sharp risk.

method_exemplars.technique: Evaluate low-degree polynomial functional estimators from factorial moments with explicit clipping and rare-cell branching.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It shows how an approximation-theoretic minimax rule can retain an explicit sample-level implementation.

method_exemplars.technique: Choose and evaluate approximation polynomials whose degree and coefficients are calibrated to sampling noise.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination needs a certified representation whose approximation and variance guarantees survive computational compression.

open_problems.open_problem: Determine whether a best-versus-runner-up margin restriction produces a sharp transition from the unrestricted many-arm categorical optimal-value rate to parametric MSE uniformly as d and K grow.

source_refs.excerpt: Add a boundary corollary contrasting the unrestricted frontier with a named margin/gap condition
or does a different least-favorable family establish a binding obstruction there?

open_problems.why_unsolved: The unrestricted categorical problem is driven by exact and near ties, while smoothing and influence-function analyses can recover root-n behavior under stronger gap control. Prior reviewers requested a quantitative boundary, but the existing honest-adaptation run treats a binary Hölder model rather than growing discrete d and K. The first proof step that changes is the approximation-bias summation: the mass of groups with small best-versus-second-best gaps must replace worst-case tie-fan approximation, and the lower mixture must obey the same margin restriction while retaining enough indistinguishable winner switches.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A minimax MSE characterization over a precisely defined best-versus-runner-up margin class, with necessary-and-sufficient conditions on d_n,K_n and the margin parameters for O(1/n) risk and matching transition rates outside that regime.

writing_exemplar.why: It frames optimal-value estimation around smoothing a categorical-treatment maximum and the regularity gained when near ties are controlled.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Optimal value is a maximum of treatment scores -> ties obstruct ordinary differentiability -> margin conditions limit mass near tie faces -> locate the growing-d,K parametric transition.

method_exemplars.technique: Smooth the categorical maximum by softmax, debias the smoothed score, and balance smoothing bias against stochastic error.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It supplies a regular-side estimator and limit argument that the minimax boundary should recover.

method_exemplars.technique: Use margin-controlled localized alternatives and plug-in-error-to-regret conversion to obtain matching fast-rate regimes.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The same small-gap mass controls how often winner-estimation errors change the maximum functional.

open_problems.open_problem: Construct honest, dimension-uniform confidence intervals for many-arm categorical optimal value that remain valid at exact ties, boundary means, sparse groups, and unknown overlap-bounded propensities, and characterize their minimax expected length.

source_refs.excerpt: not regret of a learned policy and not uniform confidence intervals
constructing a connected interval attaining n^{-ξ} up to logarithms over the same ordered pair
it is unknown whether a fully specified multiscale interval improves the upper rate

source_refs.claim: Nondifferentiable functionals admit no locally asymptotically unbiased or quantile-unbiased estimator sequences under the paper's conditions.
source_refs.author: Keisuke Hirano and Jack R. Porter

source_refs.claim: Root-n intervals for optimal value are developed at possibly nonunique strategies in an asymptotic fixed-complexity setting.
source_refs.author: Alexander R. Luedtke and Mark J. van der Laan

source_refs.claim: Stabilized one-step inference handles maxima with a growing index set under log(p)=o(sqrt(n)), but not a sparse d-by-K causal table with random denominators.
source_refs.author: Alexander R. Luedtke and Mark J. van der Laan
source_refs.venue: Journal of the American Statistical Association

source_refs.claim: Softmax smoothing gives asymptotically linear optimal-policy-value estimators but not an all-regime minimax interval-length frontier under jointly growing d and K.
source_refs.author: Justin Whitehouse, Qizhao Chen, Morgane Austern, and Vasilis Syrgkanis

open_problems.why_unsolved: The accepted discrete result deliberately excludes coverage, while the prior honest-interval project retains a gap between its expected-length lower bound and interval construction even for binary treatment. Web results confirm the structural obstruction: exact ties make the maximum nondifferentiable, and existing stabilized or smoothed procedures impose asymptotic growth and nuisance conditions that do not account for arbitrary group masses or simultaneous d-by-K occupancy. In sparse regimes, polynomial approximation bias can be the same order as stochastic error, so calibration requires an observable bias envelope or test inversion and a matching coverage lower experiment, not merely a variance estimate or Gaussian bootstrap.
open_problems.what_a_resolution_would_look_like: A computable interval I_n with coverage at least 1-alpha uniformly over the full growing-dimensional law class and matching upper and lower bounds for worst-case expected length or squared diameter in every consistency, transition, and saturation regime.

writing_exemplar.why: It motivates inference for optimal treatment value and explains exceptional laws through clinically meaningful treatment nonresponse.
writing_exemplar.motivation_arc: Optimal individualized care is summarized by optimal value -> ties and nonresponse make that value nonregular -> growing menus and sparse groups require honest inference beyond fixed-dimensional exceptional-law methods.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt softmax smoothing, orthogonal scores, explicit smoothing-bias control, and smoothed central limit arguments.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It targets the same causal maximum, but its smoothing level must be recalibrated to the minimax d,K regimes.

method_exemplars.technique: Adapt stabilized online one-step estimation and one-sided differentiability arguments for maxima with a growing index set.
method_exemplars.why_closest: It permits growing maximized collections and nonunique maximizers, the central inferential pathology here.

method_exemplars.technique: Lower-bound honest expected length through ordered moduli and construct intervals calibrated to between-class bias.
method_exemplars.why_closest: The destination is a coverage-and-diameter frontier that need not coincide with the point-estimation frontier.

literature_map:
Luedtke and van der Laan (2016, Annals of Statistics) establish that optimal-value regularity fails at exceptional laws with nonunique optimal treatments and develop online one-step inference.
Hirano and Porter (2012, Econometrica) show a general impossibility of locally unbiased regular inference for nondifferentiable functionals, placing exact ties outside ordinary efficiency theory.
Whitehouse, Chen, Austern, and Syrgkanis (2025, arXiv:2507.11780) use softmax smoothing and orthogonal scores for optimal-policy-value inference, but do not give a joint finite-sample d,K minimax MSE frontier.
Luedtke and van der Laan (2018, JASA) treat maxima with a growing index set using stabilized one-step inference under log(p)=o(sqrt(n)).
Nguyen, Barrett, and Jun (2025, AISTATS) study passive maximum-mean estimation; HAVER gives instance-dependent MSE upper bounds and shows that the empirical maximum can be inferior.
Van Hasselt (2013) establishes opposed biases for maximum sample averages and cross-validation and shows that unbiased maximum-value estimation is unavailable in general.
D'Eramo, Restelli, and Nuara (2016, ICML) propose a Gaussian-weighted maximum-value estimator but analyze bias and variance separately rather than a global minimax MSE.
Jiao, Venkat, Han, and Weissman (2015, IEEE TIT) combine best polynomial approximation, factorial-moment estimators, and fuzzy-hypothesis lower bounds for sparse nonsmooth functionals.
Wu and Yang (2016, IEEE TIT) use polynomial duality to obtain matching all-regime entropy MSE and consistency thresholds, providing a structural template for the missing maximum-functional geometry.
Cai and Low (2011, Annals of Statistics) provide a sharp moment-matched-mixture and approximation-theoretic template for nonsmooth minimax upper and lower bounds.
Paturi (1992, STOC) characterizes approximate degree for symmetric Boolean functions; the OR slice supplies a rigorous obstruction that any low-degree K-ary maximum certificate must respect.
Zhou, Athey, and Wager (2023, Operations Research) study observational multi-action policy learning with minimax regret, but their object is learned-policy regret rather than unrestricted optimal-value MSE.
Masten (2023, Japanese Economic Review) studies minimax-regret rules with many treatments and finds that empirical success can perform poorly in unbalanced designs.
Wang, Agarwal, and Dudik (2017), Li, Munos, and Szepesvari (2015), and Kallus, Saito, and Uehara (2021) characterize fixed-policy evaluation risk or efficiency under logging, not maximized policy value.
Chernozhukov, Lee, and Rosen (2013) and Chernozhukov, Chetverikov, and Kato (2013) provide bias-correction and Gaussian-maximum tools for populated regimes, but not sparse multinomial maximum-functional minimax theory.
